knowledge_point.title: Multiplying Two Matrices When They Are Conformable

question.:question/worked-solution:

$$
\underset{2\times\boxed{{\color{#2E8B57}{2}}}}{X}\underset{{\color{#2E8B57}{\checkmark}}}{\cdot}\underset{\boxed{{\color{#2E8B57}{2}}}\times3}{Y}=\underset{2\times3}{XY}
$$

For entry $c_{11}$, use row $1$ of $X$ (blue) and column $1$ of $Y$ (red):

$$
\begin{aligned}&\begin{bmatrix}{\color{#4169E1}{2}} & {\color{#4169E1}{0}} \\ {\color{gray}{-3}} & {\color{gray}{1}}\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}{\color{red}{1}} & {\color{gray}{0}} & {\color{gray}{-4}} \\ {\color{red}{1}} & {\color{gray}{-4}} & {\color{gray}{2}}\end{bmatrix}\\ &=\begin{bmatrix}\boxed{2} & \ast & \ast \\ \ast & \ast & \ast\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}c_{11}&={\color{#4169E1}{2}}\cdot {\color{red}{1}}+{\color{#4169E1}{0}}\cdot {\color{red}{1}} \\ &=2\end{aligned}
$$

For entry $c_{12}$, use row $1$ of $X$ (blue) and column $2$ of $Y$ (red):

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}c_{12}&={\color{#4169E1}{2}}\cdot {\color{red}{0}}+{\color{#4169E1}{0}}\cdot ({\color{red}{-4}}) \\ &=0\end{aligned}
$$

For entry $c_{13}$, use row $1$ of $X$ (blue) and column $3$ of $Y$ (red):

$$
\begin{aligned}&\begin{bmatrix}{\color{#4169E1}{2}} & {\color{#4169E1}{0}} \\ {\color{gray}{-3}} & {\color{gray}{1}}\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}{\color{gray}{1}} & {\color{gray}{0}} & {\color{red}{-4}} \\ {\color{gray}{1}} & {\color{gray}{-4}} & {\color{red}{2}}\end{bmatrix}\\ &=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 0 & \boxed{-8} \\ \ast & \ast & \ast\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}c_{13}&={\color{#4169E1}{2}}\cdot ({\color{red}{-4}})+{\color{#4169E1}{0}}\cdot {\color{red}{2}} \\ &=-8\end{aligned}
$$

For entry $c_{21}$, use row $2$ of $X$ (blue) and column $1$ of $Y$ (red):

$$
\begin{aligned}&\begin{bmatrix}{\color{gray}{2}} & {\color{gray}{0}} \\ {\color{#4169E1}{-3}} & {\color{#4169E1}{1}}\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}{\color{red}{1}} & {\color{gray}{0}} & {\color{gray}{-4}} \\ {\color{red}{1}} & {\color{gray}{-4}} & {\color{gray}{2}}\end{bmatrix}\\ &=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 0 & -8 \\ \boxed{-2} & \ast & \ast\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}c_{21}&=({\color{#4169E1}{-3}})\cdot {\color{red}{1}}+{\color{#4169E1}{1}}\cdot {\color{red}{1}} \\ &=-2\end{aligned}
$$

For entry $c_{22}$, use row $2$ of $X$ (blue) and column $2$ of $Y$ (red):

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}c_{22}&=({\color{#4169E1}{-3}})\cdot {\color{red}{0}}+{\color{#4169E1}{1}}\cdot ({\color{red}{-4}}) \\ &=-4\end{aligned}
$$

For entry $c_{23}$, use row $2$ of $X$ (blue) and column $3$ of $Y$ (red):

$$
\begin{aligned}&\begin{bmatrix}{\color{gray}{2}} & {\color{gray}{0}} \\ {\color{#4169E1}{-3}} & {\color{#4169E1}{1}}\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}{\color{gray}{1}} & {\color{gray}{0}} & {\color{red}{-4}} \\ {\color{gray}{1}} & {\color{gray}{-4}} & {\color{red}{2}}\end{bmatrix}\\ &=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 0 & -8 \\ -2 & -4 & \boxed{14}\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}c_{23}&=({\color{#4169E1}{-3}})\cdot ({\color{red}{-4}})+{\color{#4169E1}{1}}\cdot {\color{red}{2}} \\ &=14\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
XY=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 0 & -8 \\ -2 & -4 & 14\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Here, $S$ is a $1\times 4$ matrix and $T$ is a $4\times 2$ matrix. The matching inner dimensions show that the product is defined, and $ST$ is $1\times 2$:

$$
\underset{1\times\boxed{{\color{#2E8B57}{4}}}}{S}\underset{{\color{#2E8B57}{\checkmark}}}{\cdot}\underset{\boxed{{\color{#2E8B57}{4}}}\times2}{T}=\underset{1\times2}{ST}
$$

For entry $c_{11}$, use row $1$ of $S$ (blue) and column $1$ of $T$ (red):

$$
\begin{aligned}&\begin{bmatrix}{\color{#4169E1}{-4}} & {\color{#4169E1}{-1}} & {\color{#4169E1}{4}} & {\color{#4169E1}{-1}}\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}{\color{red}{5}} & {\color{gray}{-5}} \\ {\color{red}{-1}} & {\color{gray}{-5}} \\ {\color{red}{1}} & {\color{gray}{-2}} \\ {\color{red}{2}} & {\color{gray}{0}}\end{bmatrix}\\ &=\begin{bmatrix}\boxed{-17} & \ast\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}c_{11}&=({\color{#4169E1}{-4}})\cdot {\color{red}{5}}+({\color{#4169E1}{-1}})\cdot ({\color{red}{-1}}) \\ &\quad +{\color{#4169E1}{4}}\cdot {\color{red}{1}}+({\color{#4169E1}{-1}})\cdot {\color{red}{2}} \\ &=-17\end{aligned}
$$

For entry $c_{12}$, use row $1$ of $S$ (blue) and column $2$ of $T$ (red):

$$
\begin{aligned}&\begin{bmatrix}{\color{#4169E1}{-4}} & {\color{#4169E1}{-1}} & {\color{#4169E1}{4}} & {\color{#4169E1}{-1}}\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}{\color{gray}{5}} & {\color{red}{-5}} \\ {\color{gray}{-1}} & {\color{red}{-5}} \\ {\color{gray}{1}} & {\color{red}{-2}} \\ {\color{gray}{2}} & {\color{red}{0}}\end{bmatrix}\\ &=\begin{bmatrix}-17 & \boxed{17}\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}c_{12}&=({\color{#4169E1}{-4}})\cdot ({\color{red}{-5}})+({\color{#4169E1}{-1}})\cdot ({\color{red}{-5}}) \\ &\quad +{\color{#4169E1}{4}}\cdot ({\color{red}{-2}})+({\color{#4169E1}{-1}})\cdot {\color{red}{0}} \\ &=17\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
ST=\begin{bmatrix}-17 & 17\end{bmatrix}.
$$
